sections.html:
North Charleston spreads across three counties, Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester, in the Lowcountry north of the city of Charleston. The Ashley River forms much of its southwest edge and the Cooper River its southeast edge. It borders Charleston, Hanahan, Goose Creek, Ladson and Summerville.

Sorting out the county comes first for any seller. It decides who assesses the property, who sends the tax bill and where the deed is recorded. Your latest bill shows which county applies to you.

The city grew around the Charleston Naval Shipyard, established in 1901, and the Naval Base that ran from 1902 to 1996. Park Circle was one of the first areas planned, in 1912, with industrial, commercial and residential sections. At incorporation the city took in Russelldale, Ferndale, Morningside, Liberty Park, Palmetto Heights, Singing Pines, Dewey Hill, Liberty Homes and John C. Calhoun Homes.

Older neighborhoods can come with aging wiring, plumbing and roofs, and a financed buyer's inspector will raise them. A cash sale does not require you to make those repairs first.

sections.h2: Flood questions that come up in a sale
sections.html:
Standing water and tidal flooding are the bigger worry in the Lowcountry. Charleston County's flood flyer urges homeowners to learn their flood zone, flood depth and flood history, because ordinary homeowners insurance generally leaves flood damage uncovered.

  • A flood policy usually begins 30 days after you buy it.
  • When the house is in a Special Flood Hazard Area and the mortgage is federally backed, flood insurance is required.
  • Elevation affects the premium, so an agent may ask for an elevation certificate.

Paperwork showing that a previous owner raised the house or lifted its equipment helps a buyer's insurer. Dig it out before you list, and keep any flood claim records with it. A buyer on a loan will ask about both.

Which school district applies hinges on the address: Charleston County School District or Dorchester School District Two. Ask the district to confirm yours rather than relying on a listing. Transit and freight connections include Charleston International Airport, rail service from Amtrak, Norfolk Southern and CSX, and CARTA buses. How long the trip is to the airport, the port or the base can shift what a street is worth, and a local agent can speak to that for your neighborhood.

sections.h2: City offices for permits and code
sections.html: The city's own pages cover Code Enforcement, Business Licenses, Zoning with an online map, Building Inspections and a Certificate of Occupancy page. If you have done work without a permit, or an open violation sits on the house, learn that before a buyer's attorney does.

Your parcel's county does the assessing. Houses in the Charleston County slice of the city follow Charleston County rules, while parcels in Berkeley or Dorchester follow theirs.

Inside Charleston County, the house you live in is assessed at 4 percent and every other kind of real estate at 6 percent. Multiply assessed value by the millage and you have the tax; a mill is a thousandth of a dollar. Residents must ask for the lower ratio by filing an application, ideally early in the year.

State law lets you pay from September 30 through January 15. Once that date is behind you, penalties of 3, 7 and 5 percent begin. August is when reassessment notices go out, and the county will quote the current appeal deadline. A sale or transfer is the one case that escapes the 15 percent cap, so the next owner's bill can differ from yours.

Real estate questions go to the county Auditor at (843) 958-4234 or RealProperty@CharlestonCounty.org. Ask whether any balance is open before you set a closing date, since the title company will want it settled.

sections.h2: Closing and recording in Charleston County
sections.html:
A Charleston County deed is filed downtown at the Register of Deeds, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200. The office opens at 8:30 a.m., closes at 5:00 p.m. on weekdays and answers at (843) 958-4800. If your house is in the Berkeley or Dorchester part of the city, the deed is recorded by that county.

Expect a state deed fee of $1.85 for every $500 of value, with an exception for estate distribution deeds. Your closing attorney can list the exact documents and affidavits your transfer requires.

A written disclosure statement is what South Carolina asks of an owner, unless the sale is exempt. Transfers by a fiduciary who administers an estate, guardianship or trust are exempt, which helps an executor selling a parent's home. Heirs selling in their own names may not qualify, and an attorney can confirm. As-is deals are also permitted by the same law.

Three things set the pace of a sale here: which county holds the parcel, whether anything is owed on the house and whether the title is clear. Start with the county, since that tells you which offices to call for a tax balance and which Register of Deeds will record the deed.

Then ask for a payoff on any mortgage and a current figure for taxes. If the house is in an estate, confirm who has authority to sign. With those answers in hand, a closing date is simple to set, and surprises are rare.

sections.h2: Selling an occupied or rental house
sections.html:
A tenant in place or an empty rental makes a traditional listing slow. Showings are hard to schedule, and a buyer using a loan expects a clean house in good condition. For those owners, comparing a cash sale of an occupied house against listing is worthwhile.

Round up the lease, the rent records and notes on repairs the tenant has requested, and be ready to describe the tenant's situation plainly.

Our team at Cash Home Buyers visits North Charleston houses wherever they stand today and writes any offer down. Whether one comes depends on the property.

If you agree, the closing date is yours to pick. No appraisal gets ordered since no bank is lending. Title work, payoffs from your proceeds and the deed filing all go through a closing attorney or title company.

To get ready, locate the newest tax bill, a mortgage payoff figure and, for inherited property, the estate papers. Name the county on the first call so the recording can be planned.

Keep your copy of the settlement statement afterward. It shows what was paid out and is the record you will want at tax time.

faqs.q: What county is North Charleston in?
faqs.a: North Charleston lies in Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester counties. Which one applies to your house decides your tax bill, assessor and Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Charleston County house in North Charleston?
faqs.a: Charleston County parcels go to the county Register of Deeds, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200, Charleston. Berkeley and Dorchester parcels are recorded in their own counties.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Probably not if you are an executor or other fiduciary handling the estate, since South Carolina exempts that transfer. Heirs selling in their own names may need to give the statement, so check with an attorney.

faqs.q: Is flood insurance required to sell a North Charleston house?
faqs.a: Not for you as the seller. The buyer needs it when the house is in a Special Flood Hazard Area and the mortgage is federally backed, and the policy usually takes 30 days to start.

faqs.q: When are North Charleston property taxes due?
faqs.a: You can pay from September 30 through January 15. After January 15, penalties of 3, 7 and 5 percent are added in steps.
